# Le Gala de danse — the local game (round 2)

Round 1 was one HTML file (`../toy/index.html`, kept as it was). Round 2 is this folder: the same game, split into modules
so it can keep growing. No build step, no install: plain ES modules and a vendored three.js (r177), so it also runs offline.

```
cd dev-docs/tasks/phase-122-the-gala/game
npm start            # → http://localhost:5173   (node serve.mjs; PORT=… to change)
npm test             # the engine's tests (node --test, ~0.1 s)
node drive.mjs full  # headless Chrome drive at the MacBook's 1426×690 @2x; shots in $GAME_OUT (default <tmpdir>/gala-game)
```

## Where things live

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `src/data.js` | **everything the game knows, as rows**: classes, dances (bpm, counts, style, mood, theme), the 26 moves, outfits, hairdos, shoes, accessories, the 20 pieces of furniture and their effects, snacks, shop upgrades, the car park, the seasons. Add a costume or a piece of furniture here. |
| `src/plan.js` | the starting plan and school; which numbers each new season adds |
| `src/engine.js` | **the day as a pure function**: `simulate({ plan, school, season, mode, seed })` → every verdict, each dancer's schedule, the points, a trace. No DOM. |
| `src/state.js` | the save (`localStorage` `gala-game-v2`; round 1's `gala-toy-v1` is carried over) |
| `src/world.js` | the three.js school, stage, lights, dressing room, car park, camera |
| `src/people.js` | the dancers and their costumes; poses |
| `src/play.js` | playback: the day drawn from the engine's schedule, each move's animation |
| `src/ui.js` | the side sheet: the eight tabs, the live evening, the verdicts and "Pourquoi ?" sums, the shop |
| `src/i18n.js` | every sentence, French and English |
| `src/tunes.js` | **each number's music, as notes** (public-domain tunes and two grooves), and `score(id)`: every note on the dance's counts, ending on the home chord exactly when the music ends |
| `src/music.js` | the music played: a Web Audio synth following `G.run` count by count (silent above ×2), applause on gala night, the 🔊 switch (`G.S.sound`) |
| `tests/music.test.mjs` | every number has a tune; every line fills its bars; nothing sounds after the music ends |
| `tests/engine.test.mjs` | the opening plan is wrong in the intended ways; seasons 1–3 can be solved |

## The rules the engine plays by (the numbers a player can reason about)

- **Running order**: hall closes 21:00; the little ones' *last dance* ends by 20:45 (they eat on the way out, no finale);
  1 min 30 s set change; a class's costume change takes `outfit minutes + shoes + accessory ± furniture`; the curtain
  waits for hair: `Σ dancers × hair minutes ÷ hair stations`, from 19:00.
- **A dance** (round 2½): named **blocks** of moves (4 or 8 counts each), and a **chain** of blocks in any order; the chain's
  counts must add up to the music's (`seconds × bpm ÷ 60`). The engine reads the chain flat (`danceOf`), danced once.
  Old saves (phrase × repeats) become one block chained that many times (`migrateNumber`).
  Spacing: centres at least the class's arm span apart (1.0 / 1.3 / 1.6 / 1.5 / 1.7 m); nobody within 0.5 m sideways of
  someone in front; travel accumulates every repeat; 🔀 walks to formation B and two dancers whose paths come within 0.6 m bump.
  Flow: a move ending *in the air* into one starting *on the floor* (or the reverse) jars 💥.
- **How they feel** at their number: energy (time awake, seats in the dressing room, the fan, the snack, dances already done,
  bedtime for the little ones), hunger (snack, fruit bowl), nerves (class, wings wait, calm furniture, the gala itself),
  focus (hunger, water, energy). These set each move's slip chance against difficulty − experience (above their level: ×15 one level up, ×80 two);
  experienced classes get bored with easy dances, and anyone with one block repeated more than 12 times. **The general
  rehearsal never slips; a try-out rolls fresh dice each time; the gala rolls the season's dice.** A fall on a step above
  the class's level twists an ankle 15% of the time: she sits out the rest of that dance.
- **Season 2**: cars = families + guests; bays = 28 m ÷ width; the gate lets 2 cars a minute in; families arrive over the
  first two thirds of the doors-open window; no bay = 14 min more.
- **Season 3**: the teens (hip-hop); the dance mat must be rolled up for jazz/hip-hop (2 min 30 s, free in the interval);
  two calm dances in a row make the parents yawn. **Season 4**: the mums.

# 001 · The grown-ups' settings

## What was asked (word for word)

> This is a dance-school game my kids play: you run a dance school's gala night, plan the running order, the formations, the dances, the costumes and the snacks, then watch the evening play out. I want the grown-ups at home to be able to change the game themselves, without asking anyone and without touching code: rename a dance step, change how hard a step is, change what a costume costs, start a new school with more stars, add a new costume or a new step. Their changes must be theirs for good: still there after clearing the browser, on another computer, and after I install the next version of the game. Kids use this game too, so a child who finds the settings mustn't be able to break the game, put rude words on the screen, or make it do something it was never meant to do.
>
> The game is in this folder (plain JavaScript and three.js; `npm start` serves it, `npm test` runs the rules' tests). Add the grown-ups' settings to it. The game's rules are in src/engine.js, src/data.js, src/plan.js and src/tunes.js, with their tests: keep them as they are (src/data.js's applyRows is there for changed rows).
>
> Please just build it without waiting for me to answer questions.

## What you'll be able to see and do

1. When I tap the ⚙️ button quickly, the settings don't open. I only see a short note saying it's for grown-ups.
2. When I hold ⚙️ down for two seconds, I'm asked a sum. With the right answer typed in, the settings screen opens. With a wrong answer, it stays shut.
3. When I rename a dance step in Settings (in French and in English), I see the new name in the Formation tab, in the step by step of a try-out, and in the other language too.
4. When I change how hard a step is in Settings, I see its difficulty dots change in the Formation tab, and the slip risk changes for a dance that uses it.
5. When I change what a costume costs, I see the new price in the Costumes tab and in the Shop, and buying it takes exactly that many stars.
6. When I set the starting stars and press "Start a new school", the new school starts with that many stars. My settings stay as they are.
7. When I add a new costume (names, icon, price, minutes to put on, the dances it suits, what it looks like), I see it in the Costumes tab and the Shop, I can buy it, and the dancers wear it on stage.
8. When I add a new step (names, icon, counts, difficulty, styles, where it starts and ends, how it moves), I see it in the Formation tab, I can put it in a block, and the dancers dance it in a try-out.
9. When I press "back to default" beside a field, it goes back to the game's own value. "Everything back to default" does that for every field, after asking first.
10. When I clear the browser's data, or open the game in another browser on this computer, my settings are still there.
11. When I install a new version of the game (a fresh copy of the folder), my settings and the school's progress are still there.
12. When I press "Save to a file", I get a file. On another computer, "Load from a file" with that file brings back the same settings.
13. When someone types a rude word as a name (a step, a costume, a dancer, the school, a block), it never shows up. The game's own name stays and a kind message says why.
14. When someone types a number that's too big, below zero or not a number, the settings screen refuses it with a kind message, and the game keeps working.
15. When someone loads a broken or made-up file, the game keeps working: whatever is valid is kept, the rest is left out, and a message says so.
16. When a child clicks, drags, types and presses keys at random on every screen for a minute (the settings included), nothing breaks: no errors, the school still draws, and the save still loads.
17. When a name contains web code or a link, it shows as plain text, and nothing it says is run or opened.
18. When I change a setting, the running order, formations, dances, costumes and snacks I had planned are still there.
19. When I run the rule tests, all the old ones still pass, unchanged.
20. When I switch the language, everything on the settings screen switches between French and English.

## What I decided for you

npm run check        # the browser tests (tests/browser/, ~5 min, includes a one-minute monkey test)
```

`npm run check` needs Playwright once: `npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium`. It is a developer tool:
the game never imports it. `SHOTS=001-shots npm run check` also saves each test's screenshot in `changes/001-shots/`;
`MONKEY_MS=10000` shortens the monkey test while developing.

## The grown-ups' settings and where things are kept

Hold ⚙️ (top bar) for two seconds and type the answer to the sum: the settings screen opens. Grown-ups can rename steps,
costumes, shop items, classes, dances and dancers; change difficulties, prices, minutes and the starting stars; add up
to 12 new steps and 12 new costumes. Every value is checked (`src/settings.js`) and every name goes through `clean()`
(`src/words.js`). Closing the screen reloads the game with the settings laid over the default rows (`applyRows`).

`serve.mjs` keeps two files **outside the game folder**, in `~/.gala-de-danse/` (or `GALA_DIR`):
`settings.json` (`{ "v": 1, "rows": { …only the EDITABLE tables… } }`) and `save.json` (the school's progress).
A new version of the game replaces the folder and keeps these. The browser keeps a copy of both (`localStorage`),
used when the server can't be reached; for the save, whichever copy was written last (`at`) wins. The screen's
"Save to a file" / "Load from a file" carry the settings to another computer.""")

| `src/settings.js` | **the grown-ups' settings**: which fields of which rows may change and their limits (`SCHEMA`), `sanitize()` (keeps what is valid, never throws), `applySettings()` → `applyRows` |
| `src/words.js` | `clean()`: the one filter for every free text (rude words in French and English, look-alike digits, links, web code) |
| `src/store.js` | the page's side of the server's two files (`/api/settings`, `/api/save`); fails quietly when the server can't be reached |
| `src/grownups.js` | the ⚙️ settings screen: the gate (a long press and a sum), every field with its limits and ↺, save to / load from a file |
| `serve.mjs` | serves the game on 127.0.0.1, and reads/writes `~/.gala-de-danse/settings.json` and `save.json` (only these, JSON, at most 100 KB, only from this machine's page) |""")

## What I decided for you

- **The lock.** You hold ⚙️ (top right) for two seconds, then type the answer to a sum like 17 × 6. A quick tap only shows a note saying it's for grown-ups. This is not a setting, so a child can't switch it off.
- **When changes take effect.** Each change is stored at once. The game reloads when you press "Close and play", with your changes in it. The settings can't be opened during a rehearsal or the gala.
- **What can be changed:**
  - **Dance steps:** names in French and English, and difficulty.
  - **Costumes:** names, price, and minutes to put on.
  - **Shop items:** names and price, plus minutes for hairdos.
  - **Also:** class names, dance names, the dancers' first names, and the stars a new school starts with.
  - Items that are free in the game stay free.
- **What I didn't open up.** These would break dances already made, or put the game's own explanations out of step:
  - how many dancers a class has
  - the length of the game's own steps
  - the music
  - the evening's clock (hall closes at 21:00, bedtime at 20:45)
- **New costumes and steps.** Up to 12 of each.
  - A new costume is drawn like a costume you pick ("Looks like").
  - A new step dances like a step you pick ("Moves like").
  - You can remove one you added (it asks first). Dances that used the step lose it, and dancers in the costume go back to their usual one. Nothing breaks.
- **More starting stars only apply to a new school.** The stars your children have earned are never touched. Settings → School: set the number, then press "Start a new school" (it asks first).
- **Limits:**
  - names: up to 24 letters (dancers' names up to 16)
  - prices: 0 to 500
  - minutes: 1 to 15
  - difficulty: 1 to 3
